Follow **CatWeb Lunar New Year Update** on Roblox, scheduled to release on February 15th: <https://www.roblox.com/events/3124291008691176052>

## Lunar New Year Update Q&A

- **How do I set up my website to use Smooth Redirects?**
> Smooth Redirects use the **Background Color** property of your **Page** as the color while redirecting. Make sure the **Background Color** is set correctly, as that color will be used on redirects!

- **My site has a background image. How do I make that work with Smooth Redirects?**
> Smooth Redirects does not currently support images. However, you can change your **Page**'s **Background Color** to the image's primary color. Color pickers can help with this.

- **Can other sites send cross-site broadcasts to my site and cause unexpected behavior?**
> No. You need to use the special **When cross-site message received...** event to receive cross-site broadcasts (When message received... will not work). This event provides the source domain name, so you can even control who you receive cross-site broadcasts from.

- **How will you implement hyphens in domain names?**
> Hyphens in domain names will be gradually rolled out to users the week after the update, similar as to how Unused Domain Claiming v2 was rolled out. They will not be available to everyone on release. To prevent impersonation, we might work with creators of top sites to reserve hyphened domain names.

messages.content:
@sneak peeks 

Since the beginning, CatWeb’s scripting system was never designed for heavy use. It was intended for simple tasks, was slow, and wasn’t built with optimization as a priority. In fact, scripting was originally considered a secondary feature that users didn’t need in order to create a site. It was built to make a button or two interactive, maybe play some music, create simple games and interactions, and other basic uses. However, you all have pushed scripting to its limits, created amazing stuff, and made scripting a core part of CatWeb.

We’ve stuck with the same scripting system until now. That changes as we rewrite the scripting system from the ground up and introduce **Script Compilation**: a system that first compiles a script into something that can be efficiently executed, instead of running directly from the raw code blocks. We've built this system with optimization as a priority so your scripts can run as fast as possible.

We're also removing the **action limit**: compiled scripts will run as fast as your CPU can handle without affecting frame rate, and in the future, will allow us to implement more features and increase limits that a fixed action limit didn't allow for. Below's a comparison on how fast the legacy interpreter can change text vs Script Compilation.

We'll be sharing more information, and hope we can release an early access form soon for those interested in trying Script Compilation at launch. Stay tuned!

-# Speed shown in the video will obviously differ on different devices and what kind of task is done.

messages.content:
@sneak peeks Broadcasting tables is getting way better with Compilation Update

Previously, tables were limited to just 5 entries. With this update, that limit is being replaced with a limit of **8 strings** (including both indexes and values), but **unlimited entries**!

We're also adding support for **nested tables**, meaning you can have tables inside other tables, making it easier to broadcast more complex data structures.

And yes, this applies to every type of broadcast, cross-site or not, across page or site, Legacy Interpreter or Script Compilation... We can't wait to see what you'll build with these new capabilities!

messages.content:
@sneak peeks

A few days ago, we released a sneak peek showing the removal of the Object Limit. Today, we'll be releasing more details on this and how limits will work on CatWeb going forward.

**We are removing the Object Limit for everyone:** The Object Limit, as well as individual event and action limits (which have been tripled) will all be replaced by one limit to the "cost" of the site. This is calculated by the number of elements, styling elements, events and actions in scripts. The limit is designed to be high enough that you should not reach it during regular use.

**What happens if I reach the Cost Limit in my site?**
> You will still be able to edit and collaborate in your site! However, you won't be able to publish it. The Editor will only stop working if you go significantly above the limit.

**What about individual limits?**
> We are tripling all individual limits:
> - **Object Limit**: 100/400 → ∞
> - **Action Limit**: 120 → 360
> - **Event Limit**: 30 → 90

**I have Premium, which increases the Object Limit to 400 for me. Since the Object Limit is being removed, what happens to this benefit?**
> You will still keep all other CatWeb Premium perks, including more pages, 3 included domains, custom themes, and more. Since the Premium Object Limit is being removed, we think it’s only fair to give Premium members early access to the new Cost Limit. While this feature will be rolled out over a few weeks, you’ll have access to it at launch with CatWeb Premium. We’ll continue adding new features and benefits to CatWeb Premium in the future.

We're excited to see what you'll build with these new limits, and we hope you are too! Stay tuned for more news on this update coming soon.
